application_guidance.input_pattern: Fresh one-point stochastic SOSP search with two independent tolerances and fixed positive scale budgets.
read_original_when: Needing finite-tolerance lower side conditions, sharp parameter interpolation, construction details or a different budget convention.
sensitive_conditions: Common loss law does not grant sample reuse.
Dimension grows within an explicit envelope.
Rich response and nu<1 extensions cannot be combined without a new theorem.

complexity_scope.guarantee: At least 2/3 success per instance, with a deterministic cap on total calls on every execution.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Fixed problem scales,nu,kappa; polylogarithmic tolerance and dimension factors suppressed.
complexity_scope.oracle: Definition 3.1 fresh gradient or HVP; Definition 3.2 rich bundle is a separate nu=1 variant.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: A point satisfying both gradient norm <=epsilon and minimum Hessian eigenvalue >=-gamma.
complexity_scope.regime: Independent sufficiently small epsilon,gamma; fixed positive problem parameters; dimension supremum up to ceil((epsilon gamma)^(-kappa)), kappa>1+2/nu.
complexity_scope.resource: Primitive fresh calls, batch size charged linearly; arithmetic and full-matrix entry materialization uncharged.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: capped DyadicSOSP_nu, Algorithm 1. Lower: arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms, unrestricted query magnitude and possibly unqueried outputs, using the paper's common scalar-loss families.

content.intended_use: Use the paper's tolerance-exponent characterization with its actual oracle and dimension envelope.

dependencies: Internal source interfaces: Lemmas A.5/A.6, Proposition A.10, Theorem A.11, Theorems F.2/F.3, Lemma F.1 and constructions cited there; external spectral routine is explicitly imported through Appendix A.4.
proofs.locator: Appendix A pp.12–17; F.2 pp.34–37; Appendix G pp.37–39
map: A.3 supplies unbiased direct random-line chords; A.5 gives simultaneous tracker accuracy. A.6 separates q times gradient drift energy from martingale curvature energy.

A.4 explicitly imports the bounded independent-matrix eigenvalue interface attributed to Arjevani et al. Lemma 16: for threshold vartheta, tilde-O((L1+barsigma2)^2/vartheta^2) fresh HVPs return either a lambda_min>=-2vartheta certificate or a unit direction of curvature <=-vartheta at prescribed conditional confidence. This external routine is an imported interface, not independently re-proved here.

Algorithm 1 and A.7–A.10 combine gradient descent, fresh signed curvature steps, gradient-count restarts, local failure coupling and deterministic physical/query caps. A.11 optimizes the anchor/drift tradeoff and absorbs epsilon^-2 gamma^-1 into the endpoint sum.

F.2 and F.3 state conservative rich-response lower endpoints. Their proofs import scalar-loss realizations and membership/activation properties from Appendices C–E and the sequential comparison Lemma F.1. Those construction proofs are not re-proved in this record.
The proof of 3.4 takes the larger of the two separate hard-instance lower bounds, at least half their sum; rich responses simulate each upper algorithm call by discarding unused entries.

G.1–G.2 rescale the existing scalar families and check population Hölder smoothness and pathwise gradient/Hessian noise, yielding curvature lower order Omega_nu(Delta sigmaH^2 L2nu^(2/nu)/(D^2 gamma^(3+2/nu))) and first-order Omega(Delta min(sigma1,sigmaH)^2/epsilon^3). Padding inactive coordinates and the kappa envelope complete 3.5; setting nu=1 gives 3.3.
proofs.omitted_details: Long lower construction proofs in Appendices B–E, the full proof of F.1 and the external eigensolver proof were not independently checked. No reconstructible Hard Family record or independent reproof is claimed.
proofs.reading_coverage: Main definitions/statements visually checked and read from original PDF pp.4–6; original-PDF pp.12–17 and34–39 read for this map. Initial pages7–9 inspected for main mechanisms.

assumptions: The random scalar loss is jointly measurable and globally C^{2,1} almost surely; F=E f and differentiation commutes with expectation through order two. No uniform sample Hessian-Lipschitz constant is prescribed.

Uniformly over deterministic x,v: E||grad f(x;Z)-grad F(x)||^2<=sigma1^2 and E||(Hess f(x;Z)-Hess F(x))v||^2<=sigma2^2||v||^2. On one common probability-one set for every x, ||Hess f(x;Z)-Hess F(x)||op<=barsigma2.

A primitive gradient/HVP call returns either grad f(x;Z) or Hess f(x;Z)v with a new independent sample drawn after x,v are chosen. The seed is neither disclosed nor reusable. Algorithms know the scale bounds and tolerances.
The rich variant is separately defined only for nu=1: one unit-cost fresh response returns (f,grad f,Hess f) jointly and additionally E|f(x;Z)-F(x)|^2<=sigma0^2 for fixed positive sigma0.

Algorithms may be randomized and adaptive; their final output need not have been queried. A budget caps all primitive calls on every path including failures; b responses cost b calls. Computation on returned data and matrix-entry counts are free.
statement.conclusion: Theorem 3.5: Tscriptstar_nu,hvp,kappa(epsilon,gamma)=tilde-Theta(epsilon^-3+gamma^(-(3+2/nu))). Theorem 3.3 specializes nu=1 to tilde-Theta(epsilon^-3+gamma^-5). Theorem 3.4: for the distinct rich model, Tscriptstar_rich,kappa(epsilon,gamma)=tilde-Theta(epsilon^-3+gamma^-5). Its explicit endpoint lower orders are Omega(Delta s0^2/epsilon^3) and Omega(Delta sigmaH^2 L2^2/(Dgamma^2 gamma^5)), where sigmaH=min(sigma2,barsigma2), s0=min(sigma0,sigma1,sigmaH), L2=L2,1, and Dgamma=2 ceil(C log(2+Delta L2^2/gamma^3+Delta sigmaH^2 L2^2/gamma^5)). The nu-Hölder HVP lower witnesses have dimensions O(Depsilon Delta/epsilon) and O_nu(Delta L2nu^(2/nu) gamma^(-(1+2/nu))), with logarithmic Depsilon. No rich-response nu<1 equality, fixed-small-d lower bound, sharp joint scale-parameter dependence or uniform vanishing-noise limit is asserted.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean R^d with induced operator norms. Fix positive Delta,L1,L2nu,sigma1,sigma2,barsigma2 and fixed nu in (0,1]. F=E f is bounded below, has initial gap F(x0)-inf F<=Delta, L1-Lipschitz gradient and nu-Hölder Hessian with constant L2nu. An (epsilon,gamma)-SOSP satisfies ||grad F(xhat)||<=epsilon and lambda_min(Hess F(xhat))>=-gamma. Tstar_nu,hvp(epsilon,gamma;d) is the least deterministic primitive-call budget achieving this with probability >=2/3 on every admissible d-dimensional instance. Define d_kappa=ceil((epsilon gamma)^(-kappa)) and Tscriptstar_nu,hvp,kappa=sup_(1<=d<=d_kappa) Tstar_nu,hvp(epsilon,gamma;d).
statement.parameter_domains: All finite dimensions for the upper bound, with only logarithmic dimension dependence; matching lower bounds within the stated growing polynomial dimension envelope. Constants may depend on fixed scale parameters,nu,kappa; tilde notation hides logarithms, never polynomial dimension factors.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: Fix all positive scale parameters and nu before taking independent positive epsilon,gamma sufficiently small. For every fixed kappa>1+2/nu the HVP equality holds. At nu=1 require kappa>3. In the rich variant also fix sigma0>0 and kappa>3. Success probability includes private algorithm and oracle randomness, is required for each instance, and uses the deterministic all-path call-budget convention.

summary: For independent small epsilon,gamma and fixed positive scales, fresh gradient/HVP minimax complexity is tilde-Theta(epsilon^-3+gamma^(-(3+2/nu))); nu=1 and the separately stated rich model have curvature exponent five.
title: Fresh common-loss SOSP tolerance frontiers
use_when: Compare fresh one-point common-loss SOSP call complexity across independent gradient and curvature tolerances.
